real_conflicts: The proposal to 'shift the title to the left or right to create asymmetrical balance' (from the composition_hierarchy verdict) is rejected. In a design dealing with 'pressure' and 'depth,' a centered, monolithic type block acts as a visual anchor—a heavy object sinking into the abyss. Asymmetry here would feel like a drift, undermining the sense of gravity and weight essential to the deep-sea theme.
accepted: The proposal to 'apply a subtle SVG gradient to the headline text' (from my own verdict) is accepted. The text must not be a flat, opaque layer. It must be a physical object within the environment, catching the cyan and purple light of the bioluminescence to prove it exists in the same space as the imagery.
concession: I concede that the current 'flat, uniform grey' is insufficient, but I reject the idea of making the text 'glow' like a neon sign. The text should not be a light source itself; it should be a solid mass illuminated by the background. The 'grain' texture proposed by the color critic should be applied to the text as well, ensuring it shares the same filmic texture as the background.
compromise: We will maintain the centered, heavy hierarchy of the headline to represent the weight of the deep ocean, but we will break the 'flatness' by applying a subtle, dark radial gradient to the text fill (lighter in the center, darker at the edges) and a faint outer glow that matches the cyan/purple background hues. This integrates the text into the lighting scheme without sacrificing the structural stability of the layout.
nonnegotiable: The headline 'BELOW THE LAST LIGHT' must remain the dominant visual element, rendered in a heavy, sans-serif weight. It must not be decorative or thin; it must feel like a physical barrier or a deep-sea vessel, commanding the space with authority.
